title: Climate Change: Causes and Evidence
text: Climate change refers to long-term shifts in global temperatures and weather patterns. Since the Industrial Revolution, human activities — primarily burning fossil fuels — have increased atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations from about 280 ppm to over 420 ppm. The greenhouse effect occurs when greenhouse gases (CO2, methane, nitrous oxide, water vapor) trap outgoing infrared radiation. Evidence for current climate change includes rising global average temperatures (about 1.1°C above pre-industrial levels), sea level rise (about 3.7 mm per year), melting ice sheets and glaciers, and shifts in species distributions. The IPCC regularly assesses the scientific evidence and projects future climate scenarios.
